rules: HM Land Registry describes INSPIRE Index Polygons as an open source dataset created to comply with the INSPIRE Directive.
The INSPIRE dataset contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE Index Polygons is a subset of HM Land Registry's wider Index Polygons database for freehold land and property.
INSPIRE polygon files are divided by local-authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both relevant local-authority files.
An INSPIRE polygon represents position and indicative extent rather than a definitive legal boundary.
Every INSPIRE Index Polygon carries a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates a polygon to a registered title.
HM Land Registry states that an INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain title registration and plan information.
The exact extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
HM Land Registry states that the individual title plan is required to identify registered-title extent.
A registered title has a single title number even when it contains several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon under a title has a separate Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can indicate that the land is not registered.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID can also indicate leasehold or another tenure omitted from the INSPIRE dataset.
HM Land Registry directs users to Search the index map to determine whether land is registered.
Business e-services customers can use MapSearch to view the full Index Polygon dataset free of charge.
INSPIRE polygons and attributes are reusable under the Open Government Licence.
HM Land Registry states that reuse under the OGL is free.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions automatically ends the rights granted under the licence.
Reuse requires acknowledgement of HM Land Registry Crown copyright and database rights.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires the specified Ordnance Survey copyright/database-right attribution.
HM Land Registry asks reusers to provide a link to the INSPIRE conditions where possible.
The INSPIRE dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly publication contains data from the previous month.
Published monthly INSPIRE files remain accessible until the following month's replacement.
HM Land Registry publishes INSPIRE data as GML files.
HM Land Registry says GIS software is required to view downloaded INSPIRE Index Polygons.
GIS software can store or edit downloaded INSPIRE data for comparison or integration with other datasets.
GML is an open data format widely used across Europe.
HM Land Registry says its GML format complies with the EU INSPIRE Directive.
HM Land Registry uses GML to provide a standard data structure across GIS and CAD systems.
HM Land Registry guidance lists ESRI Shapefile as a possible conversion target from GML.
HM Land Registry guidance lists MapInfo MIF or TAB as possible conversion targets from GML.
HM Land Registry guidance lists AutoCAD DXF as a possible conversion target from GML.
HM Land Registry guidance lists GeoJSON as a possible conversion target from GML.
HM Land Registry guidance lists KML as a possible conversion target from GML.
QGIS is identified by HM Land Registry as a free open-source application that can view and convert GML.
HM Land Registry captures polygon coordinates against British National Grid and identifies that CRS as EPSG:27700.
HM Land Registry warns that British National Grid to WGS84 conversion may shift some features by up to 15 metres.
The Planning Data API exposes planning and housing data through the /entity.{extension} search endpoint.
The entity search extension must be one of json, html or geojson.
The q parameter is documented for postcode or UPRN search.
The typology parameter can filter entity search by typology.
The dataset parameter can filter entity search by dataset.
The organisation_entity parameter can filter entity search by managing organisation.
The entity parameter can filter entity search by entity number.
The curie parameter can filter entity search by CURIE.
The prefix parameter can filter entity search by prefix.
The reference parameter can filter entity search by reference.
The period parameter can restrict results to current or all entries.
The start_date_year parameter filters by year in combination with start_date_match.
The start_date_month parameter filters by month in combination with start_date_match.
The start_date_day parameter filters by day in combination with start_date_match.
Planning Data supports coordinate queries that construct a point from supplied latitude and longitude.
Coordinate search returns entities whose geometry intersects the constructed point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied in a coordinate query.
Planning Data recommends UPRN search as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Planning Data warns that an empty query result does not prove no planning constraint exists.
Planning Data states that coverage varies by area.
Planning Data supports WKT geometry for raw spatial searches.
Planning Data states that WKT query coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
The geometry_relation parameter supports within.
The geometry_relation parameter supports equals and disjoint.
The geometry_relation parameter supports intersects and touches.
The geometry_relation parameter supports contains and covers.
The geometry_relation parameter supports coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
Large entity result sets use offset pagination.
Planning Data recommends incrementing offset by the request limit for successive pages.
Responses can expose pre-built next and previous pagination URLs.
Responses can expose pre-built first and last pagination URLs.
Planning Data documents no batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
For API portfolio screening, Planning Data documents one request per property.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting between property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, Planning Data recommends bulk dataset downloads.
Planning Data recommends local spatial intersections when screening large portfolios from bulk data.
Bulk dataset downloads are available as CSV and JSON.
Where applicable, Planning Data bulk downloads are available as GeoJSON and Parquet.
The /dataset.{extension} endpoint lists datasets and supports field and exclude_field controls.
Planning Data publishes an OpenAPI document at /openapi.json and notes that the API is still beta.
The Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM 1m is a raster elevation model.
The DTM 1m covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM 1m has 1 metre spatial resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser return.
DTM processing removes surface objects from a DSM to model the terrain surface.
Environment Agency DTM production uses bespoke algorithms for object removal.
Environment Agency DTM production also uses manual editing.
The current DTM 1m composite record describes a product produced in 2022.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest and best-resolution source is selected.
Where source data is resampled before merging, bilinear interpolation is used.
The DTM 1m composite source period begins on 6 June 2000.
The DTM 1m composite source period ends on 2 April 2022.
Metadata index catalogues identify the source survey used for a given location.
DTM 1m data is available as GeoTIFF raster data.
Survey raster data is distributed in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
DTM elevation values are represented in metres.
Published DTM heights are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The published transformation chain uses OSTN15.
The Environment Agency states individual LIDAR survey vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The DTM 1m is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The DTM 1m metadata record identifies annual update frequency.
The DTM 1m coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The DTM 1m metadata identifier is 13787b9a-26a4-4775-8523-806d13af58fc.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WMS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WCS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes a WMTS service.
The DTM 1m record exposes an OGC API Features service.
Defra states that WMS provides a summarised elevation view.
Defra states that WCS provides elevation coverage data and raw pixel values.
Defra identifies WCS as an OGC open standard for multidimensional coverage data.
Defra documents LIDAR WCS services using WCS version 2.0.1.
Defra changed composite LIDAR endpoints to remove release-year suffixes for persistent future updates.
The persistent DTM 1m WCS path is documented as /spatialdata/lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wcs.
Defra documents GeoTIFF NoData pixels with the value -3.4028235e+38.
The Coverage Metadata - Survey Data dataset is published by the Environment Agency.
The Coverage Metadata - Survey Data record exposes WMS, WFS and OGC API Features service links.
Coverage metadata files describe survey coverage rather than the numeric raster elevation itself.
Environment Agency guidance states WMS preview imagery cannot itself be queried for elevation values.
LiDAR Composite download ZIP files now use a GeoPackage spatial metadata index describing spatial location and temporal extent.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset covering Great Britain.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 grid and contour products are created from the same source terrain data.
Both grid and contour supplies use 10km-by-10km tiles.
Terrain50 tiles are identified using the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
The grid product uses regular 50 metre post spacing.
The contour product uses 10 metre interval standard contour polylines.
The contour product includes mean high water and mean low water boundaries.
The contour product includes spot heights.
OS Terrain 50 is available as ASCII grid data.
OS Terrain 50 grid supply includes GML 3.2.1 metadata/support data.
Contour supply is available in GML 3.2.1.
Contour supply is available in Esri Shapefile.
Contour supply is available in GeoPackage.
Contour supply is available as MBTiles vector tiles.
OS Terrain 50 access is available as a download.
OS Terrain 50 OpenData access is free through the OS Data Hub.
The product can be downloaded without registration.
The national tiled supply contains 2,858 10km tiles arranged into 55 100km grid-square folders.
The national compressed grid supply is documented at approximately 157 MB.
OS Terrain 50 is designed for annual full-tile resupply.
Grid height values are calculated at pixel centres.
Grid tiles do not overlap.
Grid tiles do not share common edge values.
ASCII grid rows run from west to east.
Each ASCII grid row contains 200 pixels.
Each grid pixel measures 50 metres by 50 metres.
OS Terrain 50 grid height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
The source terrain model is captured as a triangulated irregular network.
The source TIN uses mass points, breaklines and/or automated photogrammetric techniques.
Grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN.
The bare-earth source model removes buildings and vegetation.
Supported structures with an air gap, such as bridges and viaducts, are excluded from the bare-earth model.
Most source heights are relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
Per-tile XML metadata follows the GEMINI metadata standard.
Per-tile metadata identifies the 10km National Grid tile reference.
OS Terrain 50 metadata identifies British National Grid EPSG:27700.
OS Terrain 50 metadata identifies Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701.
The OS Downloads API OpenData download endpoint supports area filters including National Grid square TQ.
When redirect is requested and exactly one OpenData download matches, the OS Downloads API documents an HTTP 307 redirect to the actual download.

blocked_gates.rule: The July 2026 Barnet and Enfield INSPIRE entries are indexed, but exact public GML href bytes and SHA remain unavailable because direct page fetch redirects loop.
Exact HMLR INSPIRE IDs and native-BNG containment for all three real candidates remain unresolved.
Exact parameterised Planning Data coordinate responses for the three candidate points remain blocked by execution URL safety.
Exact Planning Data result binding for parcel refs 52040420, 52213916 and 52213412 remains absent.
EA official product and coverage-metadata services are readable, but exact TQ2892 filtered survey-feature readback remains unavailable.
Exact candidate WCS or GeoTIFF bytes, SHA, NoData handling and numeric elevations remain absent.
Official OS Downloads API and Terrain50 supply semantics are verified, but a live Terrain50 product-details JSON readback remains absent.
OS Terrain50 TQ29 download bytes, SHA and row149 col173/174 numeric height values remain absent.
F-host recovery plus HD2 015 and HD1 016/025/identity-provenance runtime outputs remain absent.
